file_name: Chacon-Cifuentes et al. - 2020 - Interdisciplinary Approach of the Design Process for the Application of New Materials in Wheelchair.txt

barriers.description: Designers could not prototype initially in the target magnesium alloy because local access and fabrication constraints required using an alternative (aluminum) prototype first.
barriers.justification: Being unable to build prototypes in the final material limited the team's ability to produce and evaluate design solutions and delayed iterative testing of the magnesium-specific behaviors and surface treatments.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The first functional prototype is being manufactured in aluminum alloy, due to its ease of access in the local context. This prototype will be used to develop technical and usability tests.

barriers.description: Key manufacturing processes (surface treatment and powder metallurgy formation) were developed in parallel subprojects and were not yet scaled for integration into the main design process.
barriers.justification: Dependency on separately developed and not-yet-scaled subproject outputs constrained the team's ability to integrate manufacturing solutions, delaying production of the magnesium prototype and hindering evaluation and iteration workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: On the other hand, the processes for the treatment of the surfaces and the formation of pieces by powder metallurgy, were developed by materials engineers in parallel sub-projects. The results of these subprojects will be integrated into the design process when said manufacturing processes are scaled for their application in the magnesium prototype.
